description: An interactive harmonic sequencer: sixteen chords played in turn by an internal clock, with a six by sixteen grid choosing which notes of the chord now playing the arpeggio sounds

params.text: Sets how many of the sixteen chords the sequence plays before returning to the first, 1 to 16
Sets how many columns of the arpeggio grid are played within each chord, 1 to 16; the chord's time is divided evenly between them
Sets the octave of the chord now selected, 0 to 8, with 4 putting the root at 0V; selecting another chord brings that chord's own octave here
Sets the internal tempo, 1 to 300 BPM, which is the rate the sequence moves from one chord to the next
Sets the root note of its own chord in twelve steps, C at the bottom to B at the top; clicking it also makes that chord the selected one, and it is frozen for chords beyond the CHORDS LEN setting

inputs.text: A rising edge past 1V starts the sequence when it is stopped and stops it when it is running
A rising edge past 1V returns the sequence to the first chord and the first column of the arpeggio grid

outputs.text: The notes of the arpeggio column now playing, 1V per octave, one channel per cell switched on in that column; a column with none on holds the pitches of the last column that had some
A 10V gate on each channel of the arpeggio pitch output, lasting the first 85% of each column and staying at 0V for a column with no cells switched on
The chord now playing as three polyphonic channels of 1V per octave: root, third and fifth
A 10V gate on three polyphonic channels while the sequence runs, dropping to 0V for 5ms at each change of chord so the next chord gets a fresh edge
The root note of the chord now playing, on its own, 1V per octave
A 5ms pulse at 10V each time the sequence moves on to the next chord, and 0V while the sequence is stopped

notes: nothing moves until RUN is switched on. The module comes up stopped, and the clock output and both gate outputs rest at 0V until then.
there is no clock input. BPM sets the rate of the chords, and ARP LEN divides each chord into that many arpeggio steps.
the round button under a chord slider selects that chord. Clicking it again, once it is the selected one, steps that chord through major, minor, sus2, sus4, diminished and augmented.
the round chord buttons, the RUN button and the RST SEQ button are drawings rather than knobs, so clicking any of them opens no help of its own.
the arpeggio grid is one drawing rather than 96 controls, so no cell can be clicked for help. A click switches a cell on or off, and only columns within ARP LEN can be edited.
the six rows of the arpeggio grid, upwards from the bottom, are the root, third and fifth of the chord and those same three an octave higher.
Ctrl-click a grid cell to show a note name for about a second. The name is that note in the chord whose number matches the column, not the chord being played.
the RUN button starts and stops the sequence, and the RST SEQ button returns it to the first chord and the first arpeggio column.
K-SCENE goes immediately to the right of this module and stores and recalls its whole setup.
menu: Clear ARP Matrix — switches every cell of the arpeggio grid off and returns to its first column, leaving the chords alone
Clear Chords — puts every chord back to a C major at octave 4 and returns to the first chord, leaving the arpeggio grid and the two length knobs alone

inputs.0:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.

outputs.4: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
